messages:
Tessa Morgan: Dropping latest risk badge exploration for Suggestions table + drawer. Need quick eyes on copy + color contrast before we lock for beta. Figma: https://figma.com/file/console-suggestions-risk-badge-v3 (WIP)

Kenji Nakamura: Looking now. Copy question: are we calling it just “Risk” in the column header? I worry people will read it as security/compliance risk.

Marissa Cole: +1. In PM reviews people keep asking “risk of what?” We need it to be clearly perf/reliability risk.

Alicia Perez: Visually: current scheme is green/yellow/red pill with white text. I’m pretty sure the yellow w/ white text fails WCAG AA for normal text (and maybe even large depending on shade).

Tessa Morgan: Yeah that’s what I’m worried about. We can’t ship something that’s only color-coded either.

Jean-Paul Laurent: Agree. Also we should avoid “High Risk” as a scary label without context. Can we do “Higher latency risk” or “Performance risk: High”? Something that forces the read.

Kenji Nakamura: Proposal for header + badge:
- Column header: “Perf risk” (with info tooltip: “Likelihood of latency/reliability regression if applied without staged rollout.”)
- Badge text remains Low/Med/High, but the tooltip is explicit: “Performance/reliability risk, not security risk.”

George Mbatha: From the pilot interviews (last week), “risk” alone triggered security concerns twice. People asked “does this mean data risk?” so +1 to “Performance risk” as the explicit term.

Nora Ahmed: From implementation perspective, shorter header is nicer but we can do “Perf risk” with tooltip easily. Badge component can include an icon too (e.g., triangle for Medium/High) so it’s not just color.

Alicia Perez: On colors: if we keep semantic colors, we should switch to dark text on lighter background for contrast. Or use an outline pill + colored dot/icon. Right now yellow background + white text is ~1.8:1 in the mock (fails).

Tessa Morgan: What if we do:
- Low: neutral gray pill w/ “Low” + check icon
- Medium: amber outline + amber icon, dark text
- High: red outline + red icon, dark text
And keep the full words “Low/Medium/High” (no abbreviations) to help scanning.

Kenji Nakamura: I like outline + icon. We should also make sure in dark mode the outline is still visible.

Alicia Perez: I can run contrast checks for both themes. If we use tokens, we can pick from our accessible palette set.

Marissa Cole: Copy nuance: “Medium” is always weird. Could we do “Moderate”?

George Mbatha: In usability sessions, “Moderate” tested slightly worse (people asked “moderate compared to what”). “Medium” was understood as “in the middle” but they wanted the tooltip explanation.

Jean-Paul Laurent: We also need tooltip copy to be consistent with docs. Suggest something like:
“Performance risk estimates the chance this change increases p95 latency or reduces reliability for this route. Use staged rollout + monitoring.”

Kenji Nakamura: + include staleness/confidence somewhere? Or is that separate.

Tessa Morgan: Confidence is a separate column in the table (per DES-611) but risk tooltip can include a second sentence: “Risk is based on recent traffic patterns; always validate with canary.”

Nora Ahmed: UX detail: tooltips on badges can be hard on keyboard. Maybe we do a small info icon next to column header (tooltip there), and keep badge tooltip optional.

Alicia Perez: Accessibility: yes—hover-only tooltips on every cell is painful. One header tooltip + details drawer explanation is better.

Marissa Cole: Can we also avoid red/green dependency? Icon + text solves some, but color-blind folks still need shape differences.

Tessa Morgan: We can do different icons per level:
- Low: check-circle
- Medium: alert-circle
- High: alert-triangle
And keep the outline color as secondary.

Kenji Nakamura: I’ll update copy in the drawer too. Right now it says “Risk is High” without the “performance” qualifier.

George Mbatha: Strongly recommend the drawer callout header reads “Performance risk” not “Risk level”. That’s what people anchor on.

Alicia Perez: Quick note: if we use alert-triangle, ensure the icon has enough contrast too (not just thin stroke). Also avoid relying on yellow triangle alone.

Nora Ahmed: I’ll sanity check with our icon set + sizes. If we standardize to 12px icon + 12-13px text, we should be ok.

Tessa Morgan: Decisions (unless objections):
1) Rename column header to “Perf risk” with tooltip explaining it’s latency/reliability risk (not security).
2) Badge style: outline pill + dark text + icon; no white text on colored fills.
3) Drawer language uses “Performance risk” everywhere.

Marissa Cole: Works for me.

Kenji Nakamura: +1. I’ll push updated copy variants in Figma in ~1h.

Alicia Perez: I’ll run WCAG checks (AA) for light + dark and propose token values. Will comment in Figma with pass/fail.

George Mbatha: I can add this as a specific question in next usability script: “What does performance risk mean?” and see if tooltip resolves it.

Nora Ahmed: Once Figma is updated, I’ll sync with ENG on the badge component (PR-21983) so we don’t hardcode colors.

Tessa Morgan: Action items:
- Kenji: update header + tooltip copy + drawer wording by EOD.
- Alicia: contrast audit + token recommendations (light/dark) by tomorrow AM.
- Nora: confirm component supports icon + outline + keyboard-accessible tooltip pattern.
- George: add risk comprehension check to study plan.

Jean-Paul Laurent: Also please add a one-liner under tooltip: “Apply via canary rollout” + link in drawer to Rollouts docs. Helps with education.

Tessa Morgan: Good call, I’ll incorporate (reactions: :thumbsup: from Marissa Cole, :eyes: from Nora Ahmed)
